headline: Same-store growth slows; buybacks lift EPS, guidance raised
summary_short: Invitation Homes grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 9.7% y/y to $747.6M and net income 55.3% y/y to $218.8M ($0.37 diluted EPS), as same-store NOI rose a slower 1.5% on 2.7% blended rent growth and 97.1% occupancy.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.7% y/y to $747.6M and net income rose 55.3% to $218.8M ($0.37 diluted EPS), aided by NOI growth, homebuilding revenue from the ResiBuilt acquisition, and a lower diluted share count after $600M of buybacks since December. Same-store NOI grew a slower 1.5% y/y as 1.6% core revenue growth (occupancy down 20bp to 97.1%) outpaced 1.9% expense growth; blended rent growth was 2.7% (renewal 3.3%, new lease 1.1%). Long-term debt rose 4.3% y/y to $8.53B after a $500M note offering; cash was $75.8M. Invitation Homes raised FY2026 Core FFO/AFFO per-share guidance midpoints by $0.01 to $1.95 and $1.65, and raised disposition guidance by $300M to $850M.

drivers.explanation: Same Store Core Revenue growth (+1.6% y/y) was primarily driven by a 2.0% rise in average monthly rent, partly offset by a 20bp occupancy decline.
Total revenue also includes $49.5M of new homebuilding revenue from the January 2026 ResiBuilt acquisition, absent from the prior-year quarter.
Per-share metrics were lifted by NOI growth, $600M of share repurchases since December 2025, and the ResiBuilt acquisition, per management's Core FFO commentary.

FY2026 Core FFO and AFFO per-share guidance midpoints were raised $0.01 each to $1.95 and $1.65 on year-to-date performance; disposition guidance was raised $300M to $850M on favorable private-market home valuations.
